chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari, from Abdul Malik ibn Amr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I buy food, then I measure it, and with me is one who has witnessed the measuring, and I measured it for myself. So he says to me, 'Sell it to me', so I sell it to him with that measurement which I measured out.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell food measured for personal use if a witness is present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of selling food based on a witnessed measurement taken for personal use, resolving the legal nuance between the intent of consumption and the validity of the transaction. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the reliability of witness testimony in commercial contracts, ensuring transparency and preventing disputes over quantity. The ruling underscores the flexibility within fiqh to accommodate practical market needs while maintaining strict adherence to evidentiary standards.
